newsitem.title: GREECE: FRAUD CHARGES LAID AGAINST GREEK PYRAMID SCHEMES.
newsitem.headline: FRAUD CHARGES LAID AGAINST GREEK PYRAMID SCHEMES.

text.p: A public prosecutor in the northern Greek city Salonica charged a man behind two collapsed get-rich-quick pyramids with fraud on Wednesday, the state-run Athens News Agency said.
Thousands of northern Greeks are believed to have participated in the schemes, known as "Golden" and "Silver", whose estimated turnover was tens of millions of drachmas, it added.

Last week Albanians staged demonstrations in Tirana and other major cities blaming President Sali Berisha's government for the loss of their savings through the collapse of widespread pyramid investment schemes.

The Salonika prosecutor said 10,215 people had registered in one of the schemes in November 96 and turnover had reached 66 million drachmas but players who reached the top of the pyramid got no profits.
Salonika police chief Kostas Economou was quoted by the agency as saying he had asked the prosecutor not to charge the thousands of players as accomplices because "it would create a social problem."
No trial date has been set. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
